chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayoub, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We want to hasten the travel, and it was the night of departure when I asked him, so at which hour should we depart?'
So he said to me: 'As for the second day, do not depart until the sun declines, and it was the night of departure.'
And as for the third day, when the sun whitens (rises fully), then depart upon the Blessings of Allah.
So whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him.
Had He remained silent [about the latter part], no one would have remained except that he would have hastened, but He said: 'and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him'.
ai.seo_question: What are the correct times to depart from Mina on the second and third days of Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the second day of Tashriq, where early departure is permitted, and the third day, where delaying until full sunrise is preferred to maintain order among pilgrims. He explicitly links this practice to Quran 2:203, clarifying that while both haste and delay are religiously valid, the Prophet’s guidance prevents chaos by encouraging those who wish to stay longer to do so. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing divine flexibility with practical wisdom in ritual observance.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Dawood Bin Al Nu’man, from Abu Ayoub who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We wanted to hasten the travel, and it was the night departure, where I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So which time should we depart?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘As for the second day, so do not depart until the sun (starts to) decline, and it was the night of departure;
and as for the third day, so when the sun whitens, so depart upon the Blessings of Allahazwj, for Allahazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Praise is Saying [2:203]
then whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him.
Had heazwj Remained Silent, no one would have remained except that he would have hastened, but Heazwj Said and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dawud ibn al-Nu’man from abu Ayyub who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about departure and it was the night of departure. We like to be quick. What time should we depart?
He (the Imam) said, ’You must not depart on the second day before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime), it was the night of departure.
On the third day when the sun is bright white, you can depart with the blessing of Allah.
Allah, most glorious is whose praise says, “Those who depart quicker in two days have not sinned and those who depart later have not sinned.” [2:203]
If He had remained quiet everyone would depart quickly but He has said, “Those who delay have not sinned.”’”
